title: Configurable Retry Decorator

visible.label: Succeeds after transient failures within max_attempts
Re-raises final exception when attempts exhausted

hidden.label: Immediate success calls function once
hidden.script:
n = 0
@retry(max_attempts=4)
def steady(x, y=10):
    global n
    n += 1
    return x + y
assert steady(5, y=2) == 7
assert n == 1

hidden.label: Preserves function name with functools.wraps
Default max_attempts works when called as @retry()
Respects exceptions filter parameter
hidden.expectedDisplay: Stops on attempt 1 for unlisted exception

hidden.label: Exact 1 attempt behaves like single call

hints: Because @retry(max_attempts=3) takes configuration arguments, retry(...) is a decorator factory that returns decorator(fn) which returns wrapper(*args, **kwargs).
Use functools.wraps(fn) on wrapper so metadata stays intact, and catch `exceptions` (defaulting to `(Exception,)`) inside a loop for range(max_attempts).
